title: 🏛️ Exams 2008–2021 · his, her, their — and, but, because ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2021) A text describes Mary's house in Liverpool, where she lives with her brother Sam. Which word from the box completes the sentence?

"Mary and Sam have different bedrooms ___ they like different colours."
questions.explanation: The second part of the sentence gives the reason for the different bedrooms, and the word that opens a reason is because. The word and joins ideas that go together, but joins ideas that are different, and because of must be followed by a noun, not by a sentence like they like different colours.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2021) In Mary's house, her brother Sam likes blue. Which word completes the sentence?

"So, ___ bed and desk are blue."
questions.explanation: The owner is Sam, one boy, so he is he and the possessive adjective is his: his bed and desk. The word her belongs to a girl, their to two owners or more, and its to a thing or an animal. The owner chooses the word, never the object.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2020) A text describes Bob, a little boy. Which word completes the sentence?

"He's tall ___ slim."
questions.explanation: Tall and slim are two features that go together, and and joins ideas that go together: tall and slim. The word because gives a reason, and nothing here explains why he is tall, while too and with cannot join two adjectives.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2020) Bob is a little boy, tall and slim, with blond hair. Which word completes the next sentence?

"___ friend Tom is also tall."
questions.explanation: The friend belongs to Bob, one boy, so the owner is he and the possessive adjective before friend is His. The word Her belongs to a girl, He is a subject pronoun that cannot stand before a noun, and Him is not a possessive word at all.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2019) A text describes Masha, a little girl who lives in Russia. Which word completes the sentence?

"She likes all animals, ___ her favourite one is the bear."
questions.explanation: The sentence puts two different ideas side by side: she likes all animals, yet one of them is her favourite. Different ideas are joined by but. The word because would give a reason, so would give a result, and then would put the two ideas in time order.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2016) Peter has two brothers. Which word completes the next sentence?

"___ names are David and John."
questions.explanation: The names belong to the two brothers together, so the possessive adjective is Their, and it stands before the noun names. The word They is a subject pronoun that cannot stand before a noun, His would name Peter alone, and They're is the short form of they are, not a possessive.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2012) Jane lives in a small house with her parents. Which word from the box completes the sentence?

"There are three rooms in her house ___ there isn't a garden."
questions.explanation: The house has three rooms, and it has no garden: the two ideas are different, so but joins them. The word and would join ideas that go together, because would make the garden missing the reason for the rooms, and so would make it the result.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2009) It's Saturday and Bill is at home. Which word completes the sentence?

"He's watching ___ favourite cartoon programme."
questions.explanation: Bill is one boy, so the owner is he and the possessive adjective is his: his favourite cartoon. The word her belongs to a girl, he is a subject pronoun that cannot stand before a noun, and our would mean that Bill is one of the owners with the speaker.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2008) A text says: "The pupils are in the classroom. Their teacher is a nice man." Which word completes the next sentence?

"___ name is Peter."
questions.explanation: The name belongs to the teacher, one man, so the possessive adjective is His. The word Her belongs to a woman and Their to the pupils, who are not the owners of the name, and He's is the short form of he is, not a possessive.
